envelope.description: Carry the functional record from the host onto the existing docs-content message

body.title: Carry the functional record from the host onto the existing docs-content message
body.summary: Append one optional field, `functionalDefinition`, to the docs-content variant of `HostToWebview` in protocol.ts, typed by INDEXING off `DocsContent['functionalDefinition']` rather than restating the record shape — so protocol → client → daemon stay one declaration deep and cannot drift. Then forward it in `openDoc` with a conditional spread placed beside the identical `degradation` spread already there, so an absent record stays an ABSENT KEY across the postMessage boundary rather than a key holding undefined. No new message type; this mirrors exactly how S001/t5 added `sections` and `degradation` to this same variant. Behaviour is unchanged after this task: the webview has no code that reads the field yet, and that is asserted rather than assumed.
acceptanceChecks: The docs-content variant in protocol.ts declares `functionalDefinition` as an indexed type off `DocsContent`, NOT as a restated record shape — a source assertion on the annotation form, so a future hand-copied shape fails the check.
Opening a document whose content carries a record posts a docs-content message whose `functionalDefinition` is the SAME object reference the client returned (no clone, no reshaping, no defaulting).
Opening a document whose content carries NO record posts a message where `'functionalDefinition' in payload` is false — an absent key, not an undefined value.
The fail-closed arm is unchanged: a content-fetch rejection still posts `blocked:true` and carries no record.

REPLACES the prior vacuous shell check (s3/t1): capture the emitted shell for a FIXED nonce before the change and assert the post-change shell is byte-identical to that captured baseline — a check that actually fails if t1 accidentally edits renderShell, the bootstrap or the mdStyle block.
Assert the webview bootstrap contains no reference to `functionalDefinition` after t1, so 'this task is data-only' is proved rather than assumed.

tests.name: t1: a client returning a record posts docs-content carrying functionalDefinition as the SAME reference, unreshaped
t1: a client returning no record posts a message with NO functionalDefinition key ('functionalDefinition' in payload === false)
t1: a content() rejection still posts blocked:true and carries no record
t1 (contract): protocol.ts types functionalDefinition by indexing off DocsContent, not as a restated shape
t1: the emitted shell is byte-identical to the captured fixed-nonce baseline, and the bootstrap references functionalDefinition nowhere
